weather.note: Original PVGIS TMY bytes are preserved. The explicit normalization changes minute 0 to 60 and singular SAVING to SAVINGS. An earlier research text copy has different bytes; its hash must not replace the canonical provider hash.

verified_limited: Native ASCII full-year shape: 3 sensors × 8,760 intervals with 4,411 solar columns, finite outputs and independent small-matrix multiplication. Non-climatic feasibility data and low exploratory settings only.
Selected-hour three-record dew-point context exactly matches all 578 annual sky RGB rows and corresponding solar definitions in eight predeclared boundary/daylight cases.
Exact piecewise-sky horizontal integral error: 0.0041024%; uniform pi L error: 0.054038%; all six orientation bins exact; solar cosine and blocked-beam checks pass.
Equal-solid-angle direct transmission with 1,024 and 4,096 rays passes all eleven finite-disc aperture points at elevated radiance. The 256-ray profile fails one offset edge.
Angle-dependent glass direct transmission agrees with the explicit engine beam at 0, 30 and 60 degrees within 0.000724%.

A 128-positive-source, 24-sensor solar transport measurement took 350.160 seconds with a sampled child peak working set of 7,798,784 bytes. Positive-source count scaling estimates 3.08 hours for annual shipping solar alone; this is not an annual measurement.

Full-year MF4 diffuse/ground ASCII sky generation produced 226,165,911 bytes in 38.579 seconds, with sampled child peak working set 249,835,520 bytes. This fits the 512 MiB scratch file limit; nine unusually-bright sky warnings are retained.

Corrected Rust adapter completed 8,760 × 24 finite nonnegative lux values in 317.948 s under concurrent verification load. Peak child working set 68,231,168 B; sampled runner-plus-child 78,712,832 B; whole scratch peak 136,546,918 B. It emitted 3,733,872 of 108,404,736 finite-disc rays across 106 bounded batches. This establishes resource feasibility, not numerical acceptance.

Actual shared-service A/B shipping exports each replayed all 8,760 × 24 values through the same frozen CLI with zero observed lux differences. Caller wall times were 341.539 and 343.217 seconds. This is integration verification, not independent physical validation; the old executable did not report replay memory or scratch telemetry.

Separate horizontal-overhang and detached-context edge fixtures passed all 36 checks at 1,024 and 4,096 finite-disc samples. Independent projected-disc quadrature (16,384 to 65,536 slices) changed by at most 1.986914e-7 relative; maximum error/tolerance was 0.103019. This establishes only finite direct visibility, not diffuse transport, glazing or arbitrary-building accuracy.

An exploratory explicit-solar A candidate with MF2 diffuse sampling of 262,144, solar sampling of 4,096 and 1,024 finite-disc rays passes all 12 retained hours and all 288 sensor values against older ab9/ad131072 matched references with 4,096 finite rays; maximum error/tolerance is 0.797649. The lower solar2,048 candidate fails one winter value. New actual-grid A/B references and annual convergence remain required.

A non-gray east half-hemisphere test validates two groups of 64 repeated primary records: analytical maximum relative error 0.00012457 and -c64 versus f64 average maximum relative error 2.09e-7; each group contains 13 distinct native RGB results. At B interval 8512 sensor s000023, repeated ad 8,192 × 256 rcontrib and f64-averaged rtrace agree within 0.000087 lx, while receiver scales 100 and 10,000 agree at the tested point. These establish limited accumulation/scale behavior, not full-grid or annual acceptance.

At B interval 8512 sensor s000023, scaled contribution bins with negative ray depth -16 gave 190.4150985 lx at 1,048,576 divisions and 189.5414353 lx at 4,194,304 divisions: 0.460935% relative change, within the predeclared one-point 1% diagnostic bound. Moderate-ad repetitions gave 190.9145801 lx. This is a path-weight diagnostic only; the full-grid reference protocol and production profiles remain unaccepted.

A two-sensor B pilot completed all twelve fixed hours with moderate repeated, scaled, negative-depth diffuse coefficients and both explicit and patch-indirect solar transport. Coefficient stages took116.337 and247.160 seconds; all retained residuals were finite/nonnegative. The component comparisons are against an unqualified higher tuple and do not establish reference, full-grid or annual acceptance.
unresolved: The finite-disc corrected adapter and same-recipe full-year A/B replay have completed native execution. Independent matched-sky and final numerical profile acceptance remain outstanding.

Full-year A/B shipping/reference execution completed, but A sensor s000023 DA differs by 2.27397260 percentage points, exceeding the fixed 2-point tolerance; the other 239 metric checks and all 96 UDI partition checks passed. Installed annual UI acceptance is in progress, and final scientific profile freeze remains open.
The completed twelve-hour A high-sampling centroid investigation fails at two intervals, 1912 and 6320. It is retained as failed evidence; no subset counts as acceptance.
The direct-corrected prototype has winter reflected-solar errors exceeding tolerance. Its profile remains provisional while basis/sampling are investigated.

The MF2/ad1,048,576 full-grid coefficient diagnostic still fails six sensors at winter interval 8504 (maximum 7.74%), all without direct beam. The other three retained diagnostic hours pass. This supports investigating explicit reflected-solar transport; the fixed tolerance is unchanged.

Explicit solar sampling of 8,192 with diffuse sampling of 262,144 passes all 288 A values but fails B zero-based sensor index 15 (stable ID s000016) at interval 8512, with 19.022688 lx error versus 17.929929 lx allowance. Its complete failed record is retained.

Full-grid diffuse sampling of 1,048,576 with explicit solar sampling of 8,192 passes all 288 A values, but B fails one value at interval 8512: stable sensor s000023 (zero-based index 22), 183.72413220000004 lx versus 193.500432 lx, with tolerance 9.6750216 lx. The earlier index 15 (s000016) failure now passes. Reference convergence at the remaining point is being investigated; no failure is rounded away.

Independent uniform-hemisphere diagnostics expose high-sampling numerical failures: rtrace errors exceed 1% at 1M, 4M and 8M ambient divisions; rcontrib unit-radiance contribution is zero at 4M/8M. At ad8192, a dimmed 0.001 sky also returns zero. Repeated moderate sampling and normalized receiver scaling are exploratory remedies; no new profile is accepted.

Scaled same-sky contribution reference at B interval 8512 sensor s000023 remains unconverged: 1,048,576 versus 4,194,304 divisions gives 188.8691113 versus 184.1996994 lx, a 2.53497% change exceeding the diagnostic 1% bound. Scales 100 and 10,000 at identical sampling give exactly the same normalized result. The residual is therefore not explained by the receiver contribution cutoff or float accumulation alone; cumulative path-weight termination is under isolated investigation.

The centroid-sun half-disc aperture check reports 0 instead of 60.830157 lx. Changing -ds cannot correct the distant-source nopart behavior.
Radiance dj1 approximate square-to-disc jitter has off-centre bias and is not selected for correction.
Equal-solid-angle 256-ray sampling fails an offset edge. The 1,024/4,096-ray passes do not alone freeze a production profile.
Complete actual-grid method2 matched references now cover twelve hours for each alternative: A and B each fail 13 of 288 sensor values, with all values retained.
